content: Compression stockings are specialized garments designed to provide support to the venous and lymphatic systems of the legs. These stockings deliver graduated compression, with the highest level of compression applied at the ankle, gradually decreasing as the stocking extends up the leg. This graduated compression, when combined with the calf muscle pump effect, facilitates the circulation of blood and lymphatic fluid throughout the legs. Modern compression stockings are available in a variety of opacities, colors, styles, and sizes, making them nearly indistinguishable from regular hosiery or socks. Indications for Use Compression stockings are commonly used for the following conditions: Tired, aching legs Varicose veins Venous insufficiency Edema (swelling) Lymphedema Burn scars Prevention of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) Compression Classes Compression stockings are constructed using elastic fibers or rubber, which exert pressure on the limb to enhance circulation. They are available in various levels of compression, measured in millimeters of mercury (mmHg). The pressure ranges are as follows: Support (over-the-counter): 10–15 mmHg 15–20 mmHg With physician advice or prescription: 20–30 mmHg 30–40 mmHg 40–50 mmHg 50+ mmHg Some manufacturers, particularly for custom-made, flat-knitted products, use additional compression levels, which are also common in Europe: 18–21 mmHg 23–32 mmHg 34–46 mmHg >50 mmHg Styles Compression stockings are available in the following styles: Knee-high (AD) Thigh-high (AG) Pantyhose (AT) Commonly Used Terms for Compression Stockings Anti-embolism stockings: These are worn by non-ambulatory or post-surgical patients to prevent blood pooling in the legs, which could lead to venous thrombosis. Custom stockings: These are uniquely tailored for an individual’s specific needs. Circular knit: Seamless stockings that are aesthetically appealing. Flat knit: Stockings made with a seam, allowing them to be constructed in virtually any shape or size. These are often used for higher compression classes. Silver stockings: These are made with special silver textile fibers, which provide natural antimicrobial protection.
